summary: Preserved PR 3145's valid V3.2 and NPU extractions and corrected its reproduced missing AMD/CPU hardware separation by adding dedicated mixins and moving AMD/CPU attention prepare/core dispatch out of deepseek_v2.py. This fixes the concrete structural counterexample, not every remaining platform branch in the broader incremental refactor.

tests.command: Run test_deepseek_hardware_mixins.py from an archive of exact candidate 8f131570f6d56fa3298720cfec2506660bfd4596
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before layout regression: deepseek_v2_amd_mixin.py was absent (1 failed, 7 passed).
Dedicated backend layout; every AMD, CPU, and NPU attention routing signature; preserved V3.2 policy and MLA dispatch (30 passed, 8 subtests passed).
Formatting, imports, lint, registered-test metadata, and repository policy checks.

tests.command: Run empty_dsa_topk on cuda:0 and compare device/dtype/shape with an independent torch.empty allocation
tests.what_was_measured: On AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, both tensors were cuda:0, torch.int32, shape (0, 17).

gpu_execution.evidence: reports/j-07c30e9c7ab1/evidence/gpu-check.log records AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 execution and the independent allocation comparison.

remaining_limitations: No real DeepSeek V3.2 checkpoint or weights: Indexer/IndexerKPool loading, logits, serving, and semantic accuracy were not exercised.
Only one GPU was assigned; no real multi-GPU or pipeline-parallel stage boundary crossed the top-k handoff.
No NPU, NVIDIA, CPU-only, or MUSA architecture-specific runtime path was executed.
AMD and CPU attention dispatch was validated with adversarial mocks; the AMD GPU check only validates the V3.2 empty-top-k tensor invariant.
Platform conditionals unrelated to attention dispatch remain in deepseek_v2.py and require their own architecture/configuration evidence before extraction.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
